summary: E73 flagged .si-state.live (L67) → --grn for audit: is 'LIVE' an admission event or runtime observation? Audit confirms semantic collision. Two operational-state classes exist: (1) .si-state.live → --grn (L67), applied to source surfaces temple.html/focus.html (L247-248) meaning 'currently serving'; (2) .si-state.active → --pur (L71), applied to skills/memories meaning 'currently in use'. Both are runtime observations (not admission events), yet they use different colors. Per E73 boundary: --grn = admission event occurred (operator-authorized ledger write). Temple.html/focus.html being 'live' means they are currently running HTML surfaces — a runtime health signal, not a ledger write. No --teal variable exists in :root (E69 --teal proposal never admitted). Closest existing color for an operational/active state is --pur (already used by .si-state.active for the same semantic). Proposed tweak: .si-state.live → --pur, aligning with .si-state.active and vacating --grn for admission-only use. Contrast: .si-state.shipped → --grn remains correct (claim STARSHIP_V3 was admitted to ledger, per L241).
